title: fallback inventory -- audit every module for backup paths, silent defaults, and spaghetti
author: the operator
trigger: operator directive 2026-09-09: 'I want you to propose a later set of PRDs that go through and identify fallback paths in every module and write them to a single document.' Preceded by the operator's frustration about stepping through modules and discovering 'backup paths and fallback and all sorts of other spaghetti stuff' that makes troubleshooting 'disastrously hard'. The motivation is not aesthetic -- it is that a fallback masks a real failure: try/except that returns a default instead of raising hides the bug; .get('key') on a dict returns None instead of KeyError and the next stage crashes with a confusing NoneType error; env-with-default means missing config silently degrades behavior instead of failing at boot. The PRD-V2-019 (resize), V2-020 (dead code), V2-021 (tmp paths) and V2-022 (telegram delivery) cleanup work has already shipped or is in flight -- V2-023 is the next layer: stop hiding failures.
background: v2 production code has accumulated fallback patterns across every module-domain. Some are documented (gate's MOTION_GATE_V2=1 opt-in, gate's V1/V2 routing rule 5 variants, multi-format normalizer in daemon.py), some are not (silent except branches, env-with-default for required values, optional kwargs that change behavior). The operator's stepping-through-modules review revealed that any code path can have N alternatives, making it impossible to reason about behavior from a single trace. The audit must produce a single inventory document that names every fallback, what file:line it lives at, what it does, and what the recommended fix is. NO CODE CHANGES ship in this PRD -- it is read-only and the output is a markdown file the operator uses to author the follow-up removal PRDs (V2-024 through V2-029). Scope: production source tree only -- infra/, listener/, telegram_formatter/, vehicle_matcher/. Tests, models, scripts, docs, archive, data, .venv, .git are excluded. The pattern catalog covers 12 categories (see design_principles) and the scanner (scripts/find_fallbacks.py) enforces that no new fallback can be added without tripping the regression guard.
shipping_definition: All eight US-023 stories marked done; pytest 132/132 (or higher) green; tree clean; docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md exists and contains an entry per file in the production source tree, with every entry having all 5 required fields (file:line, code excerpt, what-it-does, why-fallback, recommended-fix); scripts/find_fallbacks.py exists, runs cleanly, exits 0 on the current production tree, and exits non-zero with file:line output against a synthetic offending file; tests/test_find_fallbacks.py exists and passes; `make check-no-fallbacks` runs as part of the existing pre-push hook chain; operator has reviewed the inventory and approved the scope of follow-up removal PRDs (V2-024 through V2-029) before any removal work begins.
scope_exclusions: Removing any fallback IS NOT in this PRD -- V2-023 is read-only inventory work. Removal PRDs (V2-024 through V2-029) are separate documents authored after the operator reviews the inventory.

Identifying dead/unused code IS NOT in this PRD -- that's PRD-V2-020 (already shipped). V2-023 only finds LIVE code that has a fallback alternative. Dead code with no callers is not a fallback, it's dead code.

Identifying v1 surface leaks IS NOT this PRD's primary scope -- the farm-surveillance-v2 skill's legacy-surface audit procedure covers that. V2-023 does flag v1 surface as one of the 12 pattern categories, but the inventory entries for v1 leaks are flagged DEFERRED-to-v1-audit so a separate workstream owns them.
Identifying resize / JPEG / letterbox / thumbnail IS NOT this PRD -- that's PRD-V2-019 (in flight). V2-023 does flag those patterns but flags them DEFERRED-to-V2-019.
Identifying /tmp writes IS NOT this PRD -- that's PRD-V2-021 (in flight). V2-023 does flag /tmp writes but flags them DEFERRED-to-V2-021.
Identifying private-data-in-config IS NOT this PRD -- that's PRD-V2-018. V2-023 flags those entries DEFERRED-to-V2-018.
Authoring the removal PRDs (V2-024 through V2-029) IS NOT this PRD -- the operator authors those after reviewing the inventory and approving scope.
Touching tests/ code IS NOT this PRD except for adding tests/test_find_fallbacks.py in US-023h. No test-cleanup work, no assertion rewrites, no fixture changes.
Re-running coverage analysis IS NOT this PRD -- V2-020 already audited coverage. V2-023's scanner is pattern-based (regex + AST), not coverage-based.
design_principles: Pattern catalog, defined once: the 12 fallback patterns below are enumerated exhaustively. New patterns must be added to this PRD (and approved by the operator) before the scanner recognizes them. The catalog lives in the PRD so a future session knows exactly what the scanner flags.

Pattern 1 -- silent exception swallow: `try:` followed by `except` that does not `raise` and does not call `logger.exception()`. Catches and continues, hiding the real failure. Classifier: any `except \w+:` block whose body contains no `raise`, no `logger.exception`, and no `sys.exit`.

Pattern 2 -- env-with-default: `os.environ.get('X', '<default>')` where the default would silently degrade behavior. Catches: env reads with non-empty defaults that are used as a critical config (URLs, paths, ports, threshold values, model names). Exempts: env reads where the default is itself a flag like 'development'/'production', or where the value is purely informational (e.g., `os.environ.get('LOG_LEVEL', 'INFO')`).

Pattern 3 -- .get() returning fallback: `dict.get('key')` on a dict where the missing key would cause the next stage to crash with confusing NoneType error. Catches: `.get('key')` whose return value is used as if non-None without an explicit `is None` raise. Exempts: `.get('key')` calls that immediately follow with `if v is None: raise`.

Pattern 4 -- optional kwarg with branch: `def f(\w+: \w+ = None)` where the None branch picks a different code path than the non-None branch. Catches: function signatures where the default value changes which sources/strategies get used. Exempts: optional args that default to a sentinel like `_UNSET` and just pass through unchanged.

Pattern 5 -- multi-format normalizer: `normalize_<shape>()` functions where more than one normalizer exists for the same input. Catches: multiple `def normalize_` functions in the same module, OR a single normalizer with internal `if shape == X: ... elif shape == Y: ...` branches that dispatch on payload shape. Exempts: a single normalizer with one well-documented shape.

Pattern 6 -- union-type coercion: `isinstance(x, (list, str))` over union types where the branches pick a different handling path. Catches: type checks with multiple types in the isinstance tuple that branch into different code paths. Exempts: isinstance calls used for validation (raise on wrong type).

Pattern 7 -- membership fallback: `if x in container else <default>` where the default path executes when the expected value is missing. Catches: conditional expressions whose else branch returns a synthesized default instead of raising. Exempts: cases where membership IS optional (e.g., feature-flag check).

Pattern 8 -- cooldown / dedup / silent suppression: function or block named `cooldown`, `dedup`, `suppress`, `skip`, `should_skip` that returns True and causes a real event to be dropped without operator visibility. Catches: any function whose name matches the regex `^(should_)?(suppress|skip|dedup|cooldown)` AND returns a boolean used to gate pipeline stages. Exempts: the function returns the boolean for telemetry only (no gating downstream).

Pattern 9 -- Optional[] in hot signatures: type hint `Optional[X]` (or `X | None`) on parameters that are then used as if always-present. Catches: function parameters whose type hint is Optional and whose body uses the value without an explicit None check. Exempts: parameters that are documented as truly optional and have an explicit `if x is None:` branch.

Pattern 10 -- try/except broad catch: `except Exception:` or `except BaseException:` with no re-raise. Catches: bare-except or broad-except that swallows everything in its scope. Exempts: top-level main entrypoint where the broad catch is the last-resort safety net and the logger outputs the traceback.

Pattern 11 -- v1 surface in v2: any reference to a v1 module name (e.g. `infra/cooldown.py`, `infra/gate_cooldown.py`, `listener.listener._process_alert`, `normalize_flat`) inside a v2 file. Catches: docstring references, comment references, AND import statements. Catalog of v1 module names is maintained in this PRD and updated when v1 surface is found. Exempts: PRD files themselves, the `farm-surveillance-v2` skill's pitfall list (which intentionally catalogs them), and the `archive/` directory.

Pattern 12 -- resize/JPEG/letterbox: any use of `cv2.resize`, `PIL.Image.resize`, `img.thumbnail`, `letterbox`, `format='JPEG'`, `.jpg` path extension, or `quality=N` save call. Catches: all resize and JPEG quantize paths in production code. Exempts: tests/ (legitimate use for fixture size control). Catalog is shared with PRD-V2-019's scanner.

Inventory entry format is fixed: every entry has file:line, code excerpt (max 5 lines, verbatim), what-it-does (one sentence), why-fallback (one sentence tying to operator pain point), recommended-fix (specific change), assigned-to (US-XXX story ID or 'open'), status (IDENTIFIED / REMOVED / DEFERRED). DEFERRED entries name the parent PRD (DEFERRED-to-V2-019, DEFERRED-to-V2-020, etc.).

The scanner is the regression guard: scripts/find_fallbacks.py walks ONLY the production source tree and flags any match against the 12 patterns. It must exit 0 on the current production tree (after the audit has cataloged everything) and exit non-zero on a synthetic offending file. Same pattern as scripts/check_no_image_resize.py (US-019d) and scripts/check_no_private_data.py.
One story per module-domain: US-023b through US-023g each audit one domain and append to the inventory. US-023a authors the scanner + pattern catalog. US-023h wires the scanner into make/pre-push.
Operator reviews the inventory before any removal work begins: the shipping_definition includes explicit operator approval of the inventory as the gate to V2-024 through V2-029.

stories.title: author scripts/find_fallbacks.py + 12-pattern catalog + tests/test_find_fallbacks.py
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Build the static scanner that powers the V2-023 audit and the post-cleanup regression guard. (1) Write scripts/find_fallbacks.py -- a pure-stdlib scanner (no AST deps to keep it simple, regex-based) that walks ONLY the production source tree (infra/, listener/, vehicle_position/, telegram_formatter/, vehicle_matcher/) and flags any line matching one of the 12 patterns from this PRD's design_principles section. (2) Each pattern is a named regex/heuristic in a top-of-file `PATTERNS` dict so they can be enabled/disabled individually. (3) Output format: `<file>:<line>: <pattern_name>: <line_content>` -- one match per line, sorted by file then line. Exit 0 if zero matches, exit 1 if matches. (4) CLI: `python -m scripts.find_fallbacks [path]` defaults to PROJECT_ROOT. (5) tests/test_find_fallbacks.py creates a synthetic `tests/_fixtures/fallbacks_sample.py` with one example of each pattern (good for false-positive coverage) and asserts (a) the scanner returns zero matches on a known-clean file, (b) one match per pattern on a known-dirty file, (c) exit codes are correct. (6) Pattern 11 (v1 surface) requires a maintained list of v1 module names; seed it from this PRD's pitfall list and let the script read additional names from a `scripts/v1_module_names.txt` sidecar file. **Why first story:** every later story uses the scanner to find fallbacks. **Why estimate 80 LOC:** 12 regex patterns + scanner scaffolding + 12-fixture test + v1-module-name loader.
ac: AC1: scripts/find_fallbacks.py exists, is executable via `python -m scripts.find_fallbacks`, and prints `0 matches` on a known-clean tree (run against scripts/ itself, which is excluded).
AC2: `python -m scripts.find_fallbacks tests/_fixtures/fallbacks_sample.py` returns one match per pattern (12 matches for the 12 patterns) and exits 1.
AC3: tests/test_find_fallbacks.py exists and passes -- it imports scripts.find_fallbacks and asserts the 3 cases above.
AC4: pytest 132/132 (or higher) green after the change.

AC5: scripts/v1_module_names.txt exists and contains the seeded v1 module names (infra/cooldown, infra/gate_cooldown, infra/motion_types, infra/timezone, infra/vision_cache, infra/classify_schema, listener.listener, normalize_flat, /webhook route, listener._process_alert, create_app).
AC6: one commit, message 'feat(v2): US-023a -- fallback pattern scanner + 12-pattern catalog + fixtures test'.
stories.rationale: Without a scanner, the audit becomes a manual grep exercise that drifts over time. The scanner makes 'no new fallback can be added without tripping the regression guard' mechanically enforceable -- same pattern as the V2-019 no-resize and V2-018 no-private-data guards.

stories.title: audit infra/ -- append every fallback to docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Walk every .py file in infra/ using the scanner + manual review. For each match, append an inventory entry to docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md under a `## infra/` heading. (1) Run `python -m scripts.find_fallbacks infra/` to get the scanner hits. (2) For each scanner hit, write the inventory entry using the format from this PRD's design_principles. (3) Manually review the section for fallbacks the scanner missed (e.g., optional kwargs the regex missed, semantic fallbacks like `if response.status_code != 200: return None`). (4) Each entry's `assigned-to` is `open` (the operator decides which removal PRD it lands in). (5) Entries that are DEFERRED-to-V2-019 (resize/JPEG), V2-020 (dead code, already shipped), V2-021 (tmp paths), or V2-018 (private data) get status DEFERRED with the parent PRD ID. (6) Verify with `grep -c '^### ' docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md` that the count matches the scanner hit count + manual additions. **Why depends on US-023a:** the scanner is what drives the audit. **Why estimate 40 LOC:** inventory entries are short markdown bullets; the work is review and categorization, not authoring.
ac: AC1: `## infra/` heading exists in docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md.
AC2: every scanner hit from `python -m scripts.find_fallbacks infra/` has a corresponding `###` entry in the infra/ section.
AC3: every entry has all 5 required fields (file:line, code excerpt, what-it-does, why-fallback, recommended-fix) plus assigned-to and status.
AC4: DEFERRED entries name the parent PRD (DEFERRED-to-V2-019, etc.) so the operator can see scope boundaries.
AC5: pytest 132/132 (or higher) green (inventory doc doesn't affect tests).
AC6: one commit, message 'docs(v2): US-023b -- inventory all fallbacks in infra/'.
stories.rationale: infra/ is the largest and highest-risk domain -- it owns the gate, vision path, frame capture, and cooldown. The operator's pain was specifically about modules in this directory. Cataloging its fallbacks is the highest-leverage first audit.

stories.title: audit telegram_formatter/ + vehicle_matcher/ -- append every fallback to docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Same procedure as US-023b but for telegram_formatter/ and vehicle_matcher/. The dispatcher has the alert/detail/match branches; vehicle_matcher/ has the match logic against known_vehicles.json. (1) Run scanner against both directories. (2) Write inventory entries under `## telegram_formatter/` and `## vehicle_matcher/` headings. (3) Manually review for semantic fallbacks (e.g., `if 'license_plate' not in vm2_result: return None` masking a real VM2 contract violation). (4) All assigned-to `open`. **Why same story (not two):** both modules are small enough that one operator review pass covers them; splitting into two stories would be process overhead without clarity gain. **Why estimate 30 LOC:** smaller surface than infra/.
ac: AC1: `## telegram_formatter/` and `## vehicle_matcher/` headings exist in docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md.
AC2: every scanner hit from `python -m scripts.find_fallbacks telegram_formatter/ vehicle_matcher/` has a corresponding entry.
AC3: every entry has all 7 fields populated (the 5 required + assigned-to + status).
AC4: DEFERRED entries name the parent PRD where applicable.
AC5: pytest 132/132 (or higher) green.
AC6: one commit, message 'docs(v2): US-023c -- inventory all fallbacks in telegram_formatter/ and vehicle_matcher/'.
stories.rationale: telegram_formatter is the user-visible dispatch path -- any fallback here directly affects what the operator sees in their chat. vehicle_matcher is the false-positive/noisy-alert lever -- a fallback here is the difference between a useful alert and a useless one.

stories.title: audit listener/ -- append every fallback to docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Same procedure as US-023b/c but for listener/ (daemon.py + pipeline.py). The daemon has the webhook entrypoint + payload normalizers; pipeline.py has the 11-stage orchestration. (1) Run scanner against listener/. (2) Write inventory entries under `## listener/` heading. (3) Manually review for: env-with-default in daemon.py boot config (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID, VISION_LLM_URL); multi-format normalizer pairs in daemon.py (the documented normalize_reolink + normalize_flat pattern from the legacy audit); pipeline stage boundaries that have optional kwargs (verify_class, detail_class). (4) All assigned-to `open`. **Why same estimate as 023c:** listener/ has 2 files but they are the highest-traffic paths, so review is intensive.
ac: AC1: `## listener/` heading exists in docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md.
AC2: every scanner hit from `python -m scripts.find_fallbacks listener/` has a corresponding entry.
AC3: every entry has all 7 fields populated.
AC4: DEFERRED entries name the parent PRD where applicable.
AC5: pytest 132/132 (or higher) green.
AC6: one commit, message 'docs(v2): US-023d -- inventory all fallbacks in listener/'.
stories.rationale: listener/ is the system entrypoint and the orchestration backbone. A fallback here means a webhook can take a code path the operator never sees. The documented multi-format normalizer pair (normalize_reolink, normalize_flat) is the single largest known fallback surface in v2 -- it must be cataloged with full context.

stories.title: cross-reference inventory entries to operator-confirmed removal scope -- freeze the inventory
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** After US-023b/c/d land, the inventory has entries for every module-domain. The operator reviews the inventory and decides which entries become removal stories in V2-024 through V2-029 and which are marked DEFERRED or FALSE-POSITIVE. (1) Operator reads docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md end-to-end. (2) For each entry, the operator sets `assigned-to` to either a new US-XXX story ID (with V2-024/025/026/027/028/029 PRD reference) or marks it DEFERRED with reason or FALSE-POSITIVE with reason. (3) Once all entries have a final disposition, the inventory is FROZEN -- no new entries can be added without re-opening this story. (4) The freeze commit is this story's deliverable. **Why estimate 20 LOC:** the operator's review is the bulk of the work; the commit is metadata updates.
ac: AC1: every entry in docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md has a non-empty `assigned-to` field (US-XXX ID, DEFERRED with reason, or FALSE-POSITIVE with reason).
AC2: operator has reviewed the inventory end-to-end (verified by commit message naming the operator review date in the body).
AC3: the inventory footer contains a 'FROZEN <date>' marker so future sessions know the audit is closed.
AC4: pytest 132/132 (or higher) green.
AC5: one commit, message 'docs(v2): US-023e -- operator-approved fallback inventory FROZEN <date>'.
stories.rationale: Without an explicit freeze, the inventory becomes a moving target -- every PR could add entries, and the operator loses the ability to reason about scope. The freeze is the contract that says 'this is what we're gutting in V2-024 through V2-029'.

stories.title: freeze the inventory and author stub V2-024 through V2-029 PRD JSONs (placeholders with story counts from the frozen inventory)
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** With the inventory frozen, author the 6 removal PRD JSONs. Each JSON has the standard structure (prd_id, title, author, status, phase, plan_section, trigger, background, shipping_definition, scope_exclusions, design_principles, stories[]) but the `stories` array is generated FROM the frozen inventory's assigned-to fields. (1) For each removal PRD, list the inventory entries assigned to it. (2) Each inventory entry becomes ONE story in the removal PRD. (3) Each story has id (US-Na, US-Nb, etc.), title (the fallback name + file:line), status: todo, depends_on (sequential -- each story depends on the previous so the operator can dispatch them in order), estimate_loc (default 10), files ([the file containing the fallback, plus the test file that needs updating, plus docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md]), and a card_body_fallback with the standard sections. (4) Stories that are interdependent (e.g., remove normalize_flat requires removing /webhook route requires updating payload-shape tests) get depends_on chains; otherwise stories are independent. (5) Each removal PRD's shipping_definition states: 'all stories marked done, pytest 132/132 green, tree clean, docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md entries for this domain flipped to REMOVED with commit SHAs, scanner exits 0 on the cleaned tree'. **Why estimate 100 LOC:** 6 PRD JSONs * ~15-20 stories each, but mostly metadata -- the bulk is mechanical copy-paste from the inventory.
ac: AC1: all 6 PRD JSONs exist under docs/PHASE-V2-024 through 029.
AC2: each removal PRD's `stories` array length matches the count of inventory entries assigned to it.
AC3: each story's `files` array contains the inventory entry's file:line file plus the test file plus docs/FALLBACK-INVENTORY.md.
AC4: each PRD's shipping_definition names the inventory update (entries flipped to REMOVED) as a done-criterion.
AC5: each PRD's design_principles include 'No new fallback paths in <domain>' as a hard rule.
AC6: one commit per PRD JSON (so 6 commits), each message 'docs(v2): V2-NNN PRD -- remove <domain> fallbacks (authored from frozen V2-023 inventory)'.
stories.rationale: Without the removal PRDs authored up front, the operator has to re-author them every time they want to dispatch a fallback fix -- and the story split may not be the one the operator would have chosen. Authoring from the frozen inventory at audit-time guarantees the removal PRDs match the operator's actual review decisions.

stories.title: make check-no-fallbacks target + pre-push hook wiring
stories.card_body_fallback: **Story.** Wire the fallback scanner into the existing pre-push hook chain so future PRs can't add a fallback without tripping the regression guard. (1) Add a `check-no-fallbacks` target to the existing Makefile that runs `python -m scripts.find_fallbacks` and fails on any match. (2) Add a `check-no-fallbacks` line to the existing `.git/hooks/pre-push` script's chain (chain runs `check-no-private-data`, `check-no-image-resize`, `check-no-fallbacks`, then pytest). (3) The pre-push exit semantics: any scanner non-zero aborts the push with a clear 'fallback pattern matched: <file>:<line>:<pattern_name>' message. (4) Document the new target in the Makefile header comment. **Why estimate 15 LOC:** Makefile target + pre-push hook chain line + 2-line comment.
ac: AC1: `make check-no-fallbacks` runs the scanner and exits 0 on the current production tree (after V2-023a has cataloged everything).
AC2: `make check-no-fallbacks` exits non-zero with file:line output on a synthetic offending file dropped into infra/ then removed.
AC3: `.git/hooks/pre-push` chain runs the new scanner before pytest, in the same order as the existing checks.
AC4: pytest 132/132 (or higher) green.
AC5: one commit, message 'feat(v2): US-023g -- wire check-no-fallbacks into Makefile + pre-push hook'.
stories.rationale: The scanner alone is not enough -- it has to be enforced at push time, otherwise a future PR can add a fallback, pass tests, and ship. The pre-push hook is the existing enforcement surface for the no-private-data and no-resize invariants; adding no-fallbacks completes the trio.
